stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every field $K$ the induced map
$\Mor(\Spec(K), X) \to \Mor(\Spec(K), S)$
is injective.
\item The morphism $f$ is universally injective.
\item The morphism $f$ is radicial.
\item The diagonal morphism $\Delta_{X/S} : X \longrightarrow X \times_S X$
is surjective.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
conclusions:
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every field $K$ the induced map
$\Mor(\Spec(K), X) \to \Mor(\Spec(K), S)$
is injective.
\item The morphism $f$ is universally injective.
\item The morphism $f$ is radicial.
\item The diagonal morphism $\Delta_{X/S} : X \longrightarrow X \times_S X$
is surjective.
\end{enumerate}

reason: Use field-valued points to identify universal injectivity with radicial residue extensions and injectivity of underlying points; the diagonal criterion follows from uniqueness of points in field tensor fibres.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: A universally injective morphism is separated.
conclusions: A universally injective morphism is separated.

reason: Universal injectivity makes the diagonal topologically surjective onto the fibre product; the diagonal is therefore closed as a subset and the separatedness criterion applies.

conclusions: A base change of a universally injective morphism is universally injective.

A composition of radicial morphisms is radicial, and so the same holds
for the equivalent condition of being universally injective.
conclusions:

for the equivalent condition of being universally injective.
